analysis.title: Longevity weekly pulse #78: US health care earnings review (Transformational Innovation Opportunities (TRIO): Longevity)
key_insights: UnitedHealth (UNH) reported strong 3Q results with margins above consensus, with the most improvement in health insurance and Optum Health, the two areas of investor focus.

UNH raised 2026 full-year EPS guidance and gave initial 2027 commentary pointing to the lower end of its 13-16% long-term earnings growth range. UBS says 13% growth on the raised 2026 guidance puts implied 2027 comfortably above consensus.

UBS thinks UNH's 2027 color was a positive surprise even though investors expected better-than-consensus guidance, given the likely conservatism in the comments. UBS expects 2027 consensus to keep rising gradually.
UBS sees UNH as having one of the cleaner earnings growth outlooks for 2027 in health care, with solid visibility because 2027 Medicare Advantage (MA) rates are already known.

2028 is expected to become the next focus for UNH. MA rates will be a major driver of 2028 margins and earnings, and UBS expects CMS to release the preliminary advance rate notice in late February/early March 2027, when UNH shares could be volatile.
UNH said US medical cost trend is stabilizing after multiple years of post-pandemic acceleration. Along with higher pricing, this is helping operating margins.
Early 3Q reports from ISRG, ABT and JNJ show moderating medical device and procedure demand, consistent with UNH's commentary. UBS views most of the slowdown as company-specific.

ISRG US robotic procedure volume rose 10% y/y, modestly below expectations and below earlier 2026 y/y growth. ISRG beat consensus on revenue and earnings, helped by growth outside the US and by robotic system sales to hospitals.

ISRG sold off significantly after the close but recovered the next trading day. UBS reads strong system placements as predictive of future procedure volume because hospitals that buy more robots are expected to use them.

ABT's medical device results disappointed, especially in cardiovascular and diabetes. UBS thinks the issues are shorter term but is somewhat surprised by the expected slowing in ABT's diabetes business.

ABT cited certain pricing pressure outside the US and the lack of expanded US CGM coverage for non-insulin-dependent Medicare beneficiaries. UBS says this has implications for DexCom (DXCM), which shares the CGM market with ABT.

UBS thinks DXCM's recent clinical data, published in the New England Journal of Medicine, support expanded coverage for non-insulin-dependent patients. The timing of Medicare coverage expansion is hard to predict and is taking longer than ABT expected.
JNJ's medical device segment growth was limited by specific product issues. UBS expects JNJ's innovative medicines (pharmaceuticals) business to remain the key growth driver.

UBS stays positive on the structural growth of medical devices, citing demographics and low penetration. It says the significant 2026 valuation reset in the sector looks increasingly like a long-term opportunity.

market_movers.rationale: 3Q margins beat consensus and 2026 EPS guidance was raised. Implied 2027 growth is above consensus, and UBS calls UNH one of the cleaner health care earnings growth stories through 2027.
Beat consensus on revenue and earnings, but US procedure growth of 10% y/y was modestly below expectations. UBS sees strong system placements as predictive of future procedure volume.
Medical device results disappointed in cardiovascular and diabetes, and management signaled slowing in diabetes. UBS thinks the issues are likely shorter term.
ABT's comments on CGM coverage frame DXCM's outlook. UBS expects eventual Medicare coverage expansion to meaningfully increase CGM penetration, but timing is unknown.
Product-specific issues limited medical device growth. Innovative medicines remains the key growth driver.

sector_views.rationale: Near-term procedure demand is moderating, but demographics and low penetration support structural growth. The 2026 valuation reset is seen as a long-term opportunity.
A stabilizing medical cost trend and higher pricing are improving operating margins. UNH has clear 2027 earnings visibility.

earnings_insights: UNH 3Q 2026 (reported last week): margins above consensus, with the main improvement in health insurance and Optum Health. 2026 full-year EPS guidance was raised, with no figure given in the report.
UNH 2027 outlook: management pointed to the lower end of its 13-16% long-term earnings growth target. UBS says 13% growth on the raised 2026 guidance implies 2027 EPS comfortably above consensus.
ISRG 3Q 2026 (reported): US robotic procedure volume +10% y/y, modestly below expectations. Revenue and earnings beat consensus, helped by growth outside the US and by robotic system sales.
ABT 3Q 2026 (reported): disappointing medical device results, especially cardiovascular and diabetes. Management commentary implied slowing in diabetes.
JNJ 3Q 2026 (reported): modest deceleration in medical devices from product-specific issues. Innovative medicines remains the main growth driver.
risk_factors: UNH: regulatory oversight, higher medical costs, volatility in Optum Health value-based care assets, government regulation and reimbursement pressure.
UNH: 2028 Medicare Advantage rate uncertainty, with the CMS preliminary advance notice expected late February/early March 2027.
Medical devices: a sustained slowdown in end markets (ABT), hospital capital budget pressure that could hit near-term ISRG robot demand, and volatility in procedure volumes.
DXCM: reimbursement pressure and eventual competition or alternative technologies, plus delays in Medicare CGM coverage expansion.
ABT: litigation over infant nutritional products, which UBS believes is manageable.
Sector-wide product liability and litigation risk for medical device companies, and drug pricing and regulatory risk for pharma.
vol_and_positioning: ISRG sold off significantly after the close following its 3Q report and recovered the next trading day.

tension_points.bull_case: Demographics and low penetration support structural growth, and the 2026 valuation reset is a long-term opportunity. ISRG's strong system placements may predict future procedure volume.
tension_points.bear_case: Procedure demand is moderating across ISRG, ABT and JNJ, consistent with UNH's stabilizing medical trend. Share declines and valuation contraction hit the sector in 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Near-term procedure demand is moderating, but demographics and low penetration keep the long-term growth outlook attractive.
theme_stances.evidence: remain positive on the sector's structural growth outlook

theme_stances.key_argument: Implied 2027 guidance is comfortably above consensus, and 2027 MA rates are already known.
theme_stances.evidence: one of the cleaner earnings growth outlooks for 2027
